{{no footnotes|date=March 2018}}
In [[statistical theory]], the '''Pitman closeness criterion''', named after [[E. J. G. Pitman]], is a way of comparing two candidate [[estimator]]s for the same parameter. Under this criterion, estimator A is preferred to estimator B if the probability that estimator A is closer to the true value than estimator B is greater than one half. Here the meaning of ''closer'' is determined by the absolute difference in the case of a scalar parameter, or by the [[Mahalanobis distance]] for a vector parameter.
